assignment.title: Practical Assignment — Recreate, Reimagine & Design
assignment.description:
Welcome to another practical assignment!

Last week, you created your first design. This week, you're taking another step forward.

You've now been introduced to the principles of good design, layout, composition, hierarchy, typography, alignment, and the relationship between different visual elements.

It's time to put some of that knowledge into practice.

For this assignment, you will recreate the reference design provided below, but with your own creative interpretation.

Your goal is not to produce an exact copy. Instead, you'll study how the original design works and use what you've learned to create a different version of it.

You'll change the composition, experiment with the layout, choose your own colours, and arrange the elements in a way that makes sense to you.

The challenge is simple:

Learn from the reference. Apply the principles. Make the design your own.
assignment.instructions:
STEP 1 — STUDY THE REFERENCE DESIGN

Carefully examine the reference design provided with this assignment.

Pay attention to how the designer has arranged the different elements.

Notice the placement of the subject, the positioning of the text, the use of colours, the spacing between elements, and how your attention moves from one part of the design to another.

Think about the following questions:

- Where is the main subject positioned?
- Where is the text placed?
- How are the different elements aligned?
- Which elements attract your attention first?
- How do the colours work together?
- How does the arrangement make the design feel organized?

You don't need to write an essay answering these questions. Simply study the design and understand how its different elements work together before you begin creating yours.

STEP 2 — GET YOUR IMAGE SUBJECT

Before you begin designing, you need a suitable image to work with.

The reference design contains a human subject. You will need to source or generate an image that fits your own interpretation of the design.

One of the easiest ways to do this is by using an AI image generator.

HOW TO GET YOUR IMAGE USING AI

You can use an AI tool to generate an image based on your description or an existing reference image.

For example, you could upload the reference design and ask the AI to generate a similar subject while changing the person's appearance, clothing, or other details.

You could also describe the image you want from scratch.

For example:

"I want a realistic image of a stylish Nigerian woman wearing a fashionable outfit, posing confidently with her body slightly turned to the side. The image should have professional studio lighting and a clean, high-quality appearance. Show her full upper body, with a pose suitable for a modern fashion and lifestyle design. Send me the image in PNG format with a transparent background."

This is only an example. You can choose a different subject, outfit, pose, or visual direction depending on your creative idea.

IMPORTANT: TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND

When generating your image, request a PNG image with a transparent background.

This makes it easier to place the subject directly into your design without having to work around an unwanted background.

Always check the generated image before using it. If the background is not actually transparent, you may need to remove it using an appropriate tool.

Your subject does not have to be identical to the one in the reference. Find or generate an image that works with your creative direction.

If you already have a suitable image, you can use it instead.

P.S. Download the Photoroom app. It is an app used for removing backgrounds.

STEP 3 — CREATE YOUR OWN VERSION

Now that you have your image, open your chosen design software and begin recreating the reference design.

Use the software for your chosen pathway:

SMARTPHONE GRAPHIC DESIGN: PixelLab
PC GRAPHIC DESIGN: Adobe Photoshop

Your task is to create a design inspired by the reference while making deliberate changes to its appearance.

YOU MUST CHANGE THE FOLLOWING:

1. LAYOUT AND COMPOSITION

Do not simply place everything where it appears in the reference. Experiment with a different arrangement.

For example, you could position the subject on the right and the text on the left. You could place the subject at the bottom and arrange the text above. You could position the text at the top-right while placing the subject toward the bottom-left.

These are only suggestions. You are free to develop your own composition.

2. COLOURS

Choose a different colour combination that works with your subject and the message you want to communicate. Think about how your colours work together and whether they make the design visually appealing.

3. TEXT AND WORDING

The reference design contains text that you can use as inspiration. You may change the wording and replace the original name with a name of your choice. You can also use a different short sentence or statement that fits your design. Keep your text intentional and readable.

4. SUBJECT PLACEMENT

Decide where your subject should appear in your composition. The subject does not have to occupy the same position as in the reference. Experiment with its placement and how it relates to the text and other elements.

WHAT SHOULD REMAIN?

Although you are changing the design, your work should still demonstrate that you understood the reference and applied the design concepts taught this week. Your final result should look like your own interpretation, not an identical copy.

STEP 4 — APPLY WHAT YOU HAVE LEARNED

As you work, pay attention to the design principles introduced in your lessons.

HIERARCHY
Make sure the viewer can distinguish the most important information from the supporting text.

ALIGNMENT
Arrange your elements intentionally rather than placing them randomly.

COMPOSITION
Think about how your subject, text, and other visual elements work together within the canvas.

LAYOUT
Organize your elements in a way that creates a clear structure.

TYPOGRAPHY
Choose readable text styles and appropriate sizes for the different elements.

COLOUR
Use a colour combination that supports the overall appearance of your design.

You do not need to master every principle perfectly at this stage. The objective is to begin applying what you've learned instead of simply memorizing the concepts.

Don't just place elements on a canvas. Think about why you're placing them there.

STEP 5 — EXPERIMENT AND MAKE IT YOURS

You are not restricted to one particular layout or creative direction. You can experiment with different placements, colours, text arrangements, and subject positions.

You can make your design minimal, bold, modern, playful, elegant, or expressive.

However, don't change things randomly just to make your design look different. Your choices should contribute to the overall composition.

Remember, the reference is your starting point, not your limit.

NEED HELP?

If you encounter difficulties generating your image, using your software, arranging your elements, or completing the assignment, don't struggle alone.

You can ask questions in your Peer Buddy Group or the UCA community. You can also ask a fellow student for guidance.

Learn from one another, share ideas, and help each other solve problems.

You can also search YouTube for tutorials. The goal of UCA is to teach you how to self learn, team learn, and learn by structural assistance.

However, make sure you actively participate in creating your own design. The goal is to develop your skills through practice.

YOUR FINAL SUBMISSION

Once you have completed your design, follow these steps:

1. Export your final design as an image.
2. Post the completed design on your Instagram page or the designated social media platform for your pathway. Publishing your work is compulsory.
3. Include the following in your caption: "What I learned from UCA this week:"

Briefly explain something you learned about design principles, layout, composition, or another concept from this week's lessons. You may also include a personal declaration about your growth as a designer.

4. Copy the link to your published post.
5. Submit the link through the UCA Assignment Portal for review.

SUBMISSION DEADLINE

Assignment Period: Wednesday to Friday

Final Deadline: Friday, 11:59 PM

Your design must be published, and the link must be submitted through the Assignment Portal before the deadline.
assignment.requirements:
WHAT YOU WILL BE GRADED ON

Your assignment will be assessed based on the following:

1. COMPLETION — Did you complete the design using the provided reference?

2. LAYOUT AND COMPOSITION — Did you make deliberate changes to the arrangement of the subject and text?

3. APPLICATION OF DESIGN PRINCIPLES — Did you make an effort to apply the principles introduced in this week's lessons?

4. TYPOGRAPHY AND ALIGNMENT — Is your text readable, and have you made an effort to position your elements intentionally?

5. COLOUR AND VISUAL PRESENTATION — Did you choose colours that work together and contribute to the overall design?

6. CREATIVITY — Did you interpret the reference in your own way instead of simply copying it exactly?

7. SUBMISSION — Did you publish your work and submit the correct link before the deadline?

Remember, you are still learning. Your work does not have to be perfect, but we expect to see effort, experimentation, and evidence that you are beginning to apply what you've learned.

FINAL CHECKLIST

Before submitting, make sure:

- I studied the reference design.
- I obtained a suitable image subject.
- I created my design using my assigned software.
- I changed the original layout and composition.
- I experimented with my colour choices.
- I used my own wording or adapted the original text.
- I paid attention to hierarchy, alignment, and typography.
- I made an effort to apply the principles taught this week.
- My final design reflects my own creative interpretation.
- I exported my completed design.
- I published it on my designated social media platform.
- I included "What I learned from UCA this week:" in my caption.
- I copied the link to my published post.
- I submitted the link through the UCA Assignment Portal.
- I submitted before Friday, 11:59 PM.

THE CHALLENGE

Last week, you created your first design. This week, you're learning to make more intentional decisions.

You now have a better understanding of how design principles, layout, and composition influence the way a design looks and communicates.

Your job is to put that knowledge into practice.

Study the reference. Understand its structure. Experiment with your own ideas. Then create something different.

Don't just replicate the design. Understand it, reimagine it, and make it yours.
